source_text: Θεὸς ἦν ἐν ἀρχῇ, τὴν δὲ ἀρχὴν λόγου δύναμιν παρειλήφαμεν. Ὁ γὰρ δεσπότης τῶν ὅλων, αὐτὸς ὑπάρχων τοῦ παντὸς ἡ ὑπόστασις, κατὰ μὲν τὴν μηδέπω γεγενημένην ποίησιν μόνος ἦν· καθὸ δὲ πᾶσα δύναμις, ὁρατῶν τε καὶ ἀοράτων αὐτὸς ὑπόστασις ἦν, σὺν αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα· σὺν αὐτῷ διὰ λογικῆς δυνάμεως αὐτὸς καὶ ὁ λόγος, ὃς ἦν ἐν αὐτῷ, ὑπέστησε. Θελήματι δὲ τῆς ἁπλότητος αὐτοῦ προπηδᾷ λόγος· ὁ δὲ λόγος, οὐ κατὰ κενοῦ χωρήσας, ἔργον πρωτότοκον τοῦ πατρὸς γίνεται. Τοῦτον ἴσμεν τοῦ κόσμου τὴν ἀρχήν.Γέγονε δὲ κατὰ μερισμόν, οὐ κατὰ ἀποκοπήν· τὸ γὰρ ἀποτμηθὲν τοῦ πρώτου κεχώρισται, τὸ δὲ μερισθὲν οἰκονομίας τὴν αἵρεσιν προσλαβὸν οὐκ ἐνδεᾶ τὸν ὅθεν εἴληπται πεποίηκεν. Ὥσπερ γὰρ ἀπὸ μιᾶς δᾳδὸς ἀνάπτεται μὲν πυρὰ πολλά, τῆς δὲ πρώτης δᾳδὸς διὰ τὴν ἔξαψιν τῶν πολλῶν δᾳδῶν οὐκ ἐλαττοῦται τὸ φῶς, οὕτω καὶ ὁ λόγος προελθὼν ἐκ τῆς τοῦ πατρὸς δυνάμεως οὐκ ἄλογον πεποίηκε τὸν γεγεννηκότα. Καὶ γὰρ αὐτὸς ἐγὼ λαλῶ καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀκούετε, καὶ οὐ δήπου διὰ τῆς μεταβάσεως τοῦ λόγου κενὸς ὁ προσομιλῶν λόγου γίνομαι· προβαλλόμενος δὲ τὴν ἐμαυτοῦ φωνὴν διακοσμεῖν τὴν ἐν ὑμῖν ἀκόσμητον ὕλην προῄρημαι. Καὶ καθάπερ ὁ λόγος ἐν ἀρχῇ γεννηθεὶς ἀντεγέννησε τὴν καθ᾿ ἡμᾶς ποίησιν, αὐτὸς ἑαυτῷ τὴν ὕλην δημιουργήσας, οὕτω κἀγώ, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ λόγου μίμησιν ἀναγεννηθεὶς καὶ τὴν τοῦ ἀληθοῦς κατάληψιν πεποιημένος, μεταῤῥυθμίζω τῆς συγγενοῦς ὕλης τὴν σύγχυσιν. Οὔτε γὰρ ἄναρχος ἡ ὕλη καθάπερ ὁ θεός, οὐδὲ διὰ τὸ ἄναρχον καὶ αὐτὴ ἰσοδύναμος τῷ θεῷ· γεννητὴ δὲ καὶ οὐχ ὑπό του ἄλλου γεγονυῖα, μόνου δὲ ὑπὸ τοῦ πάντων δημιουργοῦ προβεβλημένη.
pass_a_gloss: God was in the beginning, and we have received the power of the Logos as the beginning. For the Master of all things, being Himself the substance of the universe, was alone insofar as the creation had not yet been made; but insofar as all power, of visible and invisible things, He Himself was the substance, all things were with Him; with Him, through the logical power, the Logos Himself, who was in Him, was established. By the will of His simplicity, the Logos proceeds; and the Logos, not having been separated into emptiness, becomes the firstborn work of the Father. We know this Logos to be the beginning of the world. And it came to be by division, not by cutting off; for what is cut off from the first is separated, but what is divided, having received the choice of economy, does not diminish the one from whom it was taken. Just as from one torch many fires are kindled, and the light of the first torch is not diminished by the kindling of the many torches, so also the Logos, having proceeded from the power of the Father, did not make the one who generated Him without reason. For even I myself speak and you hear, and I do not become empty of the Logos by the transmission of the Logos; but rather, I have undertaken to shape the unshaped matter in you by projecting my own voice. And just as the Logos, having been generated in the beginning, generated the creation among us, Himself creating the matter, so also I, having been reborn according to the imitation of the Logos and having made the grasp of the truth, rearrange the confusion of the kindred matter. For neither is the matter without beginning, just like God, nor is it equal in power to God because it is without beginning; but it is generated and has not come to be by any other, but only by the Creator of all things, having been projected.
pass_b_english: God existed in the beginning, and we have received the power of the Logos as our starting point. The Master of all is himself the substance of the universe. He was alone before creation came to be, yet as the substance of all power—both visible and invisible—all things existed with him. Through his rational power, the Logos who dwelt within him was established alongside him. By the will of his simplicity, the Logos proceeds, not by separation into emptiness, but becoming the Father's firstborn work. We recognize this Logos as the beginning of the world. He came forth by division, not by severance; what is severed is cut off from its source, but what is divided receives the role of economy and does not diminish the one from whom it came. Just as many fires are kindled from a single torch without lessening the first flame, so the Logos, proceeding from the Father's power, did not leave the One who generated him without reason. Even now I speak and you hear, yet I am not emptied of the Logos by transmitting it; instead, I project my own voice to give shape to the unformed matter within you. Just as the Logos, generated in the beginning, generated our creation—himself fashioning the matter—so I, reborn through imitation of the Logos and having grasped the truth, reorder the confusion of kindred matter. Matter is not without beginning like God, nor does its lack of beginning make it equal in power to God; it is generated and came to be through no other, but only through the Creator of all, having been projected by him.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex theological distinctions regarding the Logos, the nature of creation (division vs. cutting off), and the relationship between the speaker and the matter. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek text.
